children.text: This page summarizes the main families of electoral systems and the design choices that shape representation, legitimacy, and governance outcomes.
Typical goals include proportional representation, clear accountability, local geographic representation, and stable governing majorities. Tradeoffs are unavoidable.

Plurality (first-past-the-post) is simple but can distort representation. Proportional representation allocates seats by vote share. Mixed systems combine district seats with proportional compensation.
Designers balance simplicity versus expressiveness, district-based representation versus proportionality, and resilience to strategic voting.
What magnitude of districts is feasible? How will thresholds affect small parties? How will ballots be counted and audited? What is the expected voter education burden?
Ballots should minimize cognitive load while capturing voter intent. Ranking systems require clear instructions; party-list ballots benefit from strong visual grouping and candidate photos.
Tabulation methods shape transparency. Risk-limiting audits add confidence but require robust chain-of-custody procedures and clear escalation paths for discrepancies.
New Zealand uses MMP to balance local and proportional seats. Ireland uses single transferable vote to rank candidates. Germany combines district plurality with proportional lists.
District magnitude: number of seats per district. Threshold: minimum vote share to gain representation. Wasted vote: a vote that does not contribute to electing a candidate.

Typical goals include proportional representation, clear accountability, local geographic representation, and stable governing majorities. Tradeoffs are unavoidable.

Plurality (first-past-the-post) is simple but can distort representation. Proportional representation allocates seats by vote share. Mixed systems combine district seats with proportional compensation.
Designers balance simplicity versus expressiveness, district-based representation versus proportionality, and resilience to strategic voting.
What magnitude of districts is feasible? How will thresholds affect small parties? How will ballots be counted and audited? What is the expected voter education burden?
Ballots should minimize cognitive load while capturing voter intent. Ranking systems require clear instructions; party-list ballots benefit from strong visual grouping and candidate photos.
Tabulation methods shape transparency. Risk-limiting audits add confidence but require robust chain-of-custody procedures and clear escalation paths for discrepancies.
New Zealand uses MMP to balance local and proportional seats. Ireland uses single transferable vote to rank candidates. Germany combines district plurality with proportional lists.
District magnitude: number of seats per district. Threshold: minimum vote share to gain representation. Wasted vote: a vote that does not contribute to electing a candidate.

children.text: Provisional ballots are a critical safeguard mechanism that ensures eligible voters can cast a ballot even when questions arise about their registration or eligibility at the polling place. This artifact defines when provisional ballots must be issued, how they should be handled, and the verification process for counting.
No eligible voter should be turned away from the polls. When in doubt, issue a provisional ballot and resolve eligibility during the canvassing period.

Poll workers must offer a provisional ballot when: the voter name does not appear in the poll book; registration cannot be verified; required ID is missing; eligibility is challenged; the voter moved within the jurisdiction to a different precinct; or absentee records show a mail ballot was issued but the voter claims not to have voted it.

Explain the process; complete the provisional envelope with contact information and affirmation; mark the poll book with a unique identifier; allow the voter to mark the ballot privately; seal the ballot in the envelope; provide a tear-off receipt with a tracking number.

Red Team Finding #RT-042: Current procedure lacks explicit chain of custody requirements for transporting provisional ballots from polling place to central counting facility. Flagged as Critical severity.

Keep provisional ballots separate from regular ballots. Store in a designated sealed container at the polling place. Transport to the central facility with two-person escort (requirement under review per RFC #RT-042). Log chain of custody at each transfer with timestamps and signatures.

The canvassing board must verify eligibility of each provisional ballot within 7 days of the election: check the registration database; verify signature; confirm the voter did not cast another ballot; determine correct jurisdiction; accept or reject with a documented reason code.

children.text: Core duties of the Returning Officer from notice of election through declaration of result.
Publish the notice of election, receive nomination papers, and publish the statement of persons nominated within statutory deadlines.
Appoint presiding officers and poll clerks, designate polling places, and ensure ballot papers and corresponding number lists are issued securely.
Conduct the verification and count, allow agents to observe, and declare the result. Preserve ballot papers and documentation for the statutory retention period.
